'''Maurice Kleman''' (alternate spelling '''Kléman'''; 11 August 1934 – 29 January 2021) was a French [[physicist]] involved in experimental and theoretical studies of the physics of defects; he has covered various fields of research, from [[condensed matter]] to [[heliophysics]]. As an author, he has been collected by libraries worldwide.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n78066636/ |title=Kléman, Maurice |publisher=worldcat.org |accessdate=October 19, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=OBITUARY FOR MAURICE KLEMAN |url=https://www.kent.edu/amlci/news/obituary-maurice-kleman |publisher=Kent Education |access-date=4 September 2021}}</ref>

==Early life==
Kleman was born in [[Paris]] in a family of Jewish origin which was saved from the Nazi persecutions during the [[Second World War]] by the inhabitants of the village of [[Le Chambon-sur-Lignon]], [[Haute-Loire]], as many other refugees were; this village is collectively honored as [[Righteous Among the Nations]].

== Education ==
[[Ecole Polytechnique]] and [[Ecole des Mines de Paris]]; PhD under [[Jacques Friedel|J. Friedel]]’s supervision on [[Ferromagnetism|ferromagnetic]] thin films, at the French Iron and Steel Institute (IRSID). Postdoc at the [[University of Oxford]].

== Career ==
Kleman belonged to the [[Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique]] (CNRS) since 1969, first as a member of the [[Laboratoire de Physique des Solides]] (LPS) in [[Orsay]] (1969-1993), which he headed from 1982 to 1984, then of the Laboratoire de Minéralogie et de Cristallographie de Paris (LMCP). He joined the [[Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris]] (IPGP) in 2010 and has been visiting professor at the [[Ecole polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne]] and at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT).

== Research ==
Kleman’s research covers many domains, in [[materials science]] ([[liquid crystals]], [[quasicrystals]], magnetic systems, amorphous media), more recently in [[heliophysics]] (magnetic flux ropes). In all these domains his interests are concerned with the concept of defect,<ref>{{cite journal |first1=G. |last1=Toulouse |first2=M. |last2=Kleman |title=Principles of a classification of defects in ordered media |journal=Journal de Physique Lettres |volume=37 |pages=149–151 |year=1976 |issue=6 |doi=10.1051/jphyslet:01976003706014900 |name-list-style=vanc|url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/jpa-00231261/document }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |first=Philip W. |last=Anderson |title=Basic notions of condensed matter physics |publisher=Westview Press |date=1997 |isbn=0201328305 |name-list-style=vanc}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Kleman |first2=L. |last2=Michel |title=Spontaneous breaking of Euclidean invariance and classification of topologically stable defects and configurations of crystals and liquid crystals |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=40 |issue=21 |pages=1387–1390 |year=1978 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.40.1387 |name-list-style=vanc|bibcode=1978PhRvL..40.1387K |url=http://www.numdam.org/item/RCP25_1978__26__45_0/ }}</ref> in the continuation of [[Frederick Charles Frank|F.C. Frank]] and [[Jacques Friedel|J. Friedel]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.sho.espci.fr/spip.php?article80&lang=fr |title=Interview of Jacques Friedel by Hervé Arribart et Bernadette Bensaude-Vincent, 17 octobre 2001 |quote=De Gennes s’est penché sur l’étude des dislocations de ces corps. Mais c’est plutôt Maurice Kléman (laboratoire de Physique des solides d’Orsay, puis laboratoire de minéralogie et cristallographie de Jussieu) qui a développé ce domaine en liaison avec F.C. Franck.}}</ref> He demonstrated the role of curved crystal defects in the topology of frustrated systems.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Kleman |first2=J.F. |last2=Sadoc |title=A tentative description of the crystallography of amorphous solids |journal=Journal de Physique Lettres |volume=40 |issue=21 |pages=569–574 |year=1979 |doi=10.1051/jphyslet:019790040021056900 |s2cid=37002955 |name-list-style=vanc|url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/jpa-00231690/document }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first=M. |last=Kleman |title=Frustration in polymers |journal=Journal de Physique Lettres |volume=46 |issue=16 |pages=723–732 |year=1985 |doi=10.1051/jphyslet:019850046016072300 |s2cid=122033120 |name-list-style=vanc|url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/jpa-00232890/file/ajp-jphyslet_1985_46_16_723_0.pdf }}</ref> He developed with [[Jacques Friedel|J. Friedel]] the concepts of continuous defects.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=M. |last1=Kleman |first2=J. |last2=Friedel |title=Disclinations, dislocations, and continuous defects: A reappraisal |journal=Reviews of Modern Physics |volume=80 |issue=1 |pages=61–115 |year=2008 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.80.61 |name-list-style=vanc|arxiv=0704.3055 |bibcode=2008RvMP...80...61K |s2cid=119153528 }}</ref> He showed that interplanetary magnetic flux ropes can be understood as extended singularities of the vector potential.<ref>{{cite journal |first=M. |last=Kleman |title=Flux ropes as singularities of the vector potential |journal=Solar Physics |volume=290 |issue=3 |pages=707–725 |year=2015 |doi=10.1007/s11207-015-0647-6 |name-list-style=vanc|arxiv=1402.2640 |bibcode=2015SoPh..290..707K |s2cid=118565138 }}</ref>

== Awards ==
* 1975: Médaille d'argent du CNRS
* 1980: Prix de Physique Jean Ricard de la Société Française de Physique<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.sfpnet.fr/prix/prix-jean-ricard |title=Grands Prix de la Société Française de Physique}}</ref>
* 2007: Grand Prix de l’Académie des Sciences (prix du CEA)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/activite/prix/laureat_07.pdf |title=Winners of French Academy of Sciences Award 2007 |access-date=2016-06-02 |archive-date=2016-02-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201230217/http://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/activite/prix/laureat_07.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/activite/prix/s050208_palmares.pdf |title=French Academy of Sciences Award 2007 Ceremony - Reading the charts by Jean Salençon, Vice-Président de l'Académie des sciences}}</ref>
* 2018: International Honorary Member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences.
